title: Convert card payments at a rate that is never stale

blocks.text: Checkout converts card payments in foreign currencies to euros at the treasury service's rates. Last month the US dollar moved sharply one afternoon, and finance found dollar payments converted at the morning's rate for more than an hour. The old rate class has been deleted, and its replacement is half written.
Two rules come from the treasury team:

items: a payment is never converted at a rate fetched more than ten minutes before it (`MAX_AGE`);
the treasury accepts at most one call per ten minutes from this service, and one call to `allRates()` returns every currency it quotes.

blocks.text: Finish `rate(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/ExchangeRates.java` so that both hold, with as little machinery as they allow. Take the time from the `clock` you are given, never from the system clock: the tests move it by hand. The class has one caller thread. About eight lines in total, fields included.

cases.says: each currency is converted at the rate the treasury quotes for it
a currency paid in every few minutes still moves to the treasury's new rate within ten minutes
after a quiet period longer than ten minutes, the next payment uses the treasury's current rate
payments within ten minutes of a fetch do not call the treasury again
payments in several currencies share one treasury call per ten minutes

origin.section: Code Simpler Than the Requirement Is a Bug, Not KISS

concepts: When the whole list loads in one cheap call, one map and one load time, written only when the list is loaded, meet a maximum-age requirement with one call per period.
Code that drops a stated requirement is not simpler but wrong: a memo that never reloads fails the same maximum-age check as the over-built cache.
A cache that writes the time back on every hit counts its expiry from the last read, so an entry read more often than its time to live is never reloaded.
